# Materials and Methods

## Experimental Design

### Neuronal cultures
Wild-type pregnant rats were euthanized by exposure to CO2 and soaked in 70% ethanol for 5 min for sterilization. Embryonic day 16 (E16) rat fetuses were removed under sterile conditions and kept in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) on ice. 

For the preparation of serum-free medium (SFM) we use 1:2 - F12+, 1:50 - B27 and the remaining quantity is MEM.
F12+ is prepared as 50mL of: insulin (2.5μg) dissolved in 0.1N HCl (1ml), To 10mL of F12 media glucose (0.6 g) and  transferrin (100 μg/ml) are added and vortexed until nothing precipitates. To that we add putrescine (10 μm), progesterone (30 μL), selenium (0.525 μL), penstrem (20 μL). The F12+ media is filtered and a small tube is tested over night for contamination.  

Basal forebrains were dissected in PBS and dissociated in serum-free medium (SFM). Cells were counted using a hemocytometer and plated into either microfluidic chambers or Transwell filter chambers, as described below. All cultures were maintained in SFM at 37°C for 5 days in vitro (DIV) before treatment.

### Microfluidic (MF) chamber cultures

Cells were plated at a density of 75,000 cells per microfluidic (MF) chamber. The MF chambers are attached to glass coverslips in tissue culture dishes that were precoated overnight with poly-d-lysine (0.2 mg/ml). Two hundred microliters of medium was added to the soma compartment, and 100 μl of medium was maintained in the axon compartment to create a hydrostatic volume difference that drives the axons through the microgrooves into the axon compartment. The cells were maintained with this volume difference between the soma and axon compartments for 5 DIV to obtain compartmentalized BFCN cultures in which the axons and somas can be treated separately. These cultures were used for immunocytochemistry.

**Axon-specific treatment.** Treatments were applied exclusively to the axon compartment, and the soma–axon medium volume difference was maintained throughout to restrict the neurotrophins to the axons. Axons were stimulated with recombinant human proNGF (cleavage-resistant; catalog no. N-285; 20 ng/ml) and/or BDNF (TODO: concentration — not specified in Dasgupta *et al.*) for TODO: duration. Four conditions were compared: no treatment (ctrl), proNGF, BDNF, and proNGF + BDNF.

### Filter chamber cultures

For axon-specific treatment experiments, BFCNs were plated at a density of 1 × 10^6^ cells per filter chamber on the top compartment of Transwell filter inserts with a 1-μm pore size. Axons grew through the pores to the bottom compartment over 5 DIV. Compartmental separation of the filter system was validated in a prior study from our lab using 10-kDa dextran bead diffusion assays, which established that diffusion from the axon to the soma compartment is not detected until 2 hours, providing a 2-hour window for axon-specific treatments. This validation was not repeated as part of the present thesis experiments.

**Axon-specific treatment.** Recombinant human proNGF (cleavage-resistant; catalog no. N-285; 20 ng/ml) was added to the bottom (axon) compartment, with the medium volume difference maintained to restrict stimulation to the axons. In the western blot experiments, axons were treated over a time course of 30, 45, 60, and 75 min; in the ddPCR experiments, axons were treated for TODO: duration before lysis. Matched no-treatment cultures (ctrl) were processed in parallel. For APP knockdown, axons were pretreated with Penetratin-1–linked APP siRNA (siAPP; 80 nM) for 30 min before proNGF stimulation, with a luciferase siRNA used as a nonspecific control.

### Immunocytochemistry

Basal forebrain microfluidic cultures were fixed with 4% paraformaldehyde for 20 min, washed with PBS, and permeabilized with 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS for 10 min. Cells were blocked for 1 hour with 5% normal donkey serum and 1% bovine serum albumin (BSA) in PBS. Cells were then incubated overnight at 4°C with primary antibodies against p75^NTR^ (goat, 1:500) and Tau (rabbit, 1:500; TODO: clone/catalog) diluted in 1% BSA/PBS. The following day, cells were washed with PBS and incubated for 1 hour at room temperature with a primary antibody against β-tubulin III (Tuj1; mouse, 1:1000; TODO: catalog). After washing with PBS, cells were incubated for 1 hour at room temperature with species-appropriate donkey secondary antibodies: donkey anti-goat Alexa Fluor 488, donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 555, and donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 594 (all 1:10,000; Invitrogen). Coverslips were mounted on slides with DAPI Fluoromount-G to label nuclei. Images were acquired on a Zeiss LSM TODO confocal microscope at TODO×, and analyzed using ImageJ software.

### Western blot analysis

Five-DIV filter cultures were treated with proNGF, and axon and soma lysates were obtained in 40 and 60 μl, respectively, of lysis buffer composed of 90% RIPA buffer, 5% 10× protease inhibitors, and 5% 10× phosphatase inhibitors. After protein quantification, equal amounts of protein were run on a 12% polyacrylamide gel and transferred to nitrocellulose membrane. Equal protein loading was assessed by Ponceau staining, which was washed out with TBS (tris-buffered saline) with 0.05% Tween 20 (TBST) and was confirmed by re-probing the membranes with anti-actin. The membranes were blocked with 5% nonfat milk prepared in TBST for 1 hour. Membranes were then incubated with primary antibodies diluted in blocking solution. β-Actin (mouse, 1:10,000; catalog no. TODO) was incubated for 1 hour at room temperature. All other primary antibodies were incubated overnight at 4°C and included: pan-Tau (mouse, 1:1000; catalog no. TODO), pan-Tau (rabbit, 1:1000; catalog no. TODO), and the following phospho-Tau antibodies:

- **pThr181**: detects tau phosphorylated at threonine 181, a commonly used biomarker site that tracks Alzheimer's disease-related tau pathology (1:1000; catalog no. TODO)
- **AT8 (pSer202/pThr205)**: detects tau phosphorylated at serine 202 and threonine 205, a canonical neuropathology epitope used to identify early and established pathological tau (1:1000; catalog no. TODO)
- **pSer396**: detects tau phosphorylated at serine 396, a C-terminal site associated with tau pathology (1:1000; catalog no. TODO) After washing 3× 10 min with TBST, the blots were incubated with appropriate secondary antibodies for 1 hour at room temperature. The membrane was washed 3× 10 min with TBST and then scanned with the Odyssey infrared imaging system (LI-COR Bioscience). All blots shown are representative of at least three independent experiments.

### RT-PCR and ddPCR for Tau mRNA Quantification

To quantify tau mRNA levels in axon and soma compartments separately, RNA was extracted from filter chamber lysates collected after proNGF treatment or no treatment (ctrl). Soma lysates were collected in 60 µl and axon lysates in 40 µl of lysis buffer, keeping the two compartments physically separated throughout the procedure.

Primers were designed targeting a region in the 5' UTR of the rat *Mapt* mRNA that is common to both the 0N3R and 0N4R isoforms, allowing detection of total tau mRNA regardless of isoform. Before running digital droplet PCR (ddPCR), primers were first validated by conventional RT-PCR on filter chamber lysates to confirm amplification of a band of the expected size in both compartments.

Once primer functionality was confirmed, ddPCR was performed using the Bio-Rad QX200 ddPCR system with EvaGreen Supermix. Each reaction contained cDNA from soma or axon fractions, primers at the optimized concentration, and EvaGreen Supermix in a final volume of 20 µl. Droplets were generated using the QX200 droplet generator, thermocycled under the following conditions: 95°C for 5 min, 40 cycles of 95°C for 30 s / 60°C for 1 min, followed by 4°C for 5 min and 90°C for 5 min. Droplets were read on the QX200 droplet reader and analyzed using QuantaSoft software. Thresholds were set manually where automated thresholding failed, and wells with fewer than 10,000 accepted droplets were flagged as unreliable and excluded from analysis.

Beta-actin (*Actb*) was run in parallel on the same plate as a reference gene for normalization of loading differences between compartments.
